## Nova Care: Astronaut Health Monitoring Platform

Space missions can last for months or even years, making it important to keep track of astronauts' physical and mental well-being. With this in mind, we developed **Nova Care**, an astronaut health monitoring platform for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge, **“Health Monitoring for Long-Duration Missions.”**

Nova Care brings important health information together in one place. It allows users to monitor health indicators, view historical records, complete behavioural health check-ins, and receive health-related alerts. We also integrated AI-assisted baseline creation, anomaly detection, and trend analysis to help identify unusual patterns and changes over time. The platform supports real-time telemetry updates, health reports, and CSV data exports. It also provides role-based demo access for astronauts, medical officers, pilots, and engineers.

Our goal is to explore how technology can make health monitoring more organized and accessible during long-duration missions, where continuous observation and timely awareness are especially important. Nova Care is our attempt to contribute towards safer and more informed space exploration.
details:
Nova Care: Astronaut Health Monitoring Platform

Project Overview

Long-duration space missions create unique challenges for astronaut health. Astronauts may spend months or even years away from Earth, making continuous health observation and timely access to health information especially important. To address this challenge, our team developed Nova Care, a centralized astronaut health monitoring platform for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Nova Care brings together health monitoring, historical records, experimental AI-assisted analysis, behavioural health check-ins, alerts, and real-time telemetry in one platform. Our goal was to create a system that makes astronaut health information easier to access, understand, and monitor.

How Does Nova Care Work?

The platform provides a centralized dashboard where users can view astronaut health information and monitoring indicators. It also maintains historical health records, allowing changes to be observed over time.

One of the important components is our experimental AI service. It includes three implemented capabilities:

  • AI Baseline Creation: Establishes a baseline using available health data.
  • Anomaly Detection: Helps identify potentially unusual patterns in monitored data.
  • Trend Analysis: Examines historical records to estimate trends and changes over time.

Nova Care also includes behavioural health check-ins, allowing users to record and review behavioural health information. Health-related alerts help bring attention to relevant monitoring events.

For live monitoring, we integrated Socket.IO and WebSocket communication to receive and broadcast telemetry updates. Users can also access health reports and export available data in CSV format. The platform includes role-based demo access for astronauts, medical officers, pilots, and engineers.

Benefits and Intended Impact

We designed Nova Care around the idea that astronaut health information should be organized, accessible, and easier to monitor throughout a mission.

By bringing different monitoring capabilities together, the platform reduces the need to view separate information sources. Historical records provide context for understanding changes, while experimental AI-assisted analysis helps highlight patterns that may deserve attention.

Behavioural health check-ins also recognize that astronaut well-being involves more than physical indicators. Including both physical and behavioural health monitoring creates a broader view of astronaut well-being.

Our intended impact is to explore how integrated software systems can support health awareness, monitoring, and informed decision-making during long-duration space missions, particularly when astronauts are far from immediate medical support on Earth.

Technology and Tools Used

We developed Nova Care using a full-stack architecture:

Frontend

  • React
  • TypeScript
  • Vite

Backend

  • Node.js
  • Express.js
  • Socket.IO

AI Service

  • Python
  • FastAPI
  • NumPy
  • scikit-learn

Database

  • PostgreSQL
  • Neon Database

Deployment and Development

  • Render for deploying the frontend, backend, and AI service
  • Git and GitHub for version control and collaboration
  • Visual Studio Code for development

The frontend communicates with the backend, which handles application functionality and database interactions. The separate Python-based AI service handles the experimental baseline, anomaly detection, and trend analysis capabilities. Real-time telemetry updates are supported through Socket.IO.

What Makes Nova Care Creative?

Our approach combines multiple aspects of astronaut health monitoring in a single application instead of treating each capability as a separate tool.

We brought together historical health monitoring, AI-assisted pattern analysis, behavioural health check-ins, alerts, and live telemetry. We also considered the different people involved in a space mission by providing role-based demo access for astronauts, medical officers, pilots, and engineers.

Another important design decision was to keep the AI service separate from the main backend. This modular architecture makes the system easier to maintain and provides room for future improvements.

Factors Considered During Development

While developing Nova Care, we considered:

  • Long-duration mission conditions: The need to monitor health information over extended periods.
  • Physical and behavioural well-being: The importance of considering more than physical health indicators.
  • Accessibility of information: Keeping monitoring features organized in one dashboard.
  • Historical context: Making past records available to observe changes over time.
  • Real-time updates: Supporting live telemetry communication.
  • Different mission roles: Providing demo access for different users involved in astronaut health monitoring.
  • Modularity and scalability: Separating the frontend, backend, database, and AI service.
  • Responsible AI use: Treating AI outputs as experimental decision-support information rather than medical diagnoses.

Conclusion

Nova Care is our attempt to use software engineering, data processing, and machine learning concepts to address a real challenge in human space exploration. Through this project, we explored how different health monitoring capabilities can work together to support astronaut well-being during long-duration missions.

We hope Nova Care demonstrates how thoughtful technology integration can contribute to safer, more informed, and more sustainable space exploration.
